attempts.label: DRYAD:tdz08kq5d
attempts.entry_title: Phage selection and resistance-virulence trade-offs in Ralstonia solanacearum (Wang et al. 2024)
attempts.summary: The main findings largely hold up in this data: phage lowered bacterial density at both temperatures, SCVs were far more phage-resistant, grew faster, reached lower carrying capacity and lost virulence, and mucoid clones from the 25 C phage treatment lost twitching motility and virulence. The "SCVs retain ancestral-level biofilm" claim failed (all 16 SCVs formed more biofilm than the ancestor), as did the mutation count (10.07 per clone against 8.5). The RNA-seq counts (1477 genes) and defense-system changes held, but phcS and gspG did not change as the text states. Two items could not be tested: the pilB and pilM mutants (data missing) and whether the gspE and gspF mutations fall in 2 or 3 clones (the variant table does not say which clones carry which variants). The genome reads are not public, so sequencing was checked on processed tables only.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Wang, Wang, Yang, Lu, Fields, Xu, Shen, Wei and Friman (2024) on Dryad dataset tdz08kq5d, one workbook with the data behind each figure of the paper. It covers the selection experiment (bacterial and phage densities, colony types), the phage resistance, growth, twitching, biofilm and virulence of evolved clones, the variant calls of 28 sequenced clones, the phage adsorption assay and the transcriptome tables. The growth curves, per-clone variant calls, genome reads and the pilB and pilM data of Table S6 are not in the dataset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Wang et al. (2024) from Dryad dataset tdz08kq5d

outcomes.notes: Days 2 to 12, as the criterion now names them, temperature F(1, 36) = 73.989, p = 2.96e-10, as in Table S1a; mean OD600 0.5627 at 35 C against 0.2550 at 25 C. Variants, days 0 to 10 F = 70.911 and all seven days F = 74.019, both p < 1e-9, with 35 C higher. The first run asked which six of the data's seven time points enter the ANOVA; the reader's answer put days 2 to 12 in the criterion, the reading this claim had been decided on, so the outcome is unchanged and days 0 to 10 and all seven days are now variants only.
deviations: ANOVA computed in Python (statsmodels, strata as R's aov with Error(ID)) where the paper used R 3.6.3.

outcomes.notes: Days 2 to 12, phage F(1, 36) = 48.800, p = 3.43e-08; mean OD600 lower with phage by 68.4% at 25 C (0.1225 against 0.3876) and by 34.5% at 35 C (0.4454 against 0.6801). Variants, days 0 to 10 F = 57.811 and all seven days F = 48.881, with the same direction. The first run asked which six of the data's seven time points enter the ANOVA; the reader's answer put days 2 to 12 in the criterion, the reading this claim had been decided on, so the outcome is unchanged and days 0 to 10 and all seven days are now variants only.

Days 2 to 12, as the criterion now names them, temperature x phage x time F(5, 180) = 3.870, p = 0.0024, as in Table S1a; the -P minus +P difference at day 12 (0.3219 at 25 C, -0.0080 at 35 C) is below its largest earlier value (0.4362, 0.5046, day 2). With days 0 to 10 the interaction is F = 1.464, p = 0.2039 (not significant), while the differences still decline; with all seven days p = 0.0025. The first run asked which six time points enter the ANOVA and decided this claim on days 2 to 12, noting that days 0 to 10 would make it partially reproduced. The reader's answer put days 2 to 12 in the criterion and ruled out days 0 to 10, so the outcome stands on the criterion's own time points and the other two sets are variants that decide nothing. The criterion compares only the last day with the largest earlier value; at 25 C the difference is not a steady decline, falling to 0.049 on day 8 and rising to 0.322 on day 12.

Reading (a), trapezoid over days 2 to 12, 64.55% and 33.73% (F = 63.16 and 11.26 at df (1, 18)). Reading (b), trapezoid over days 0 to 12, 66.80% and 37.18%, with the paper's F of 88.77 and 15.66 at df (1, 18) (the paper prints (1, 19)). Reading (c), sum over days 2 to 12, 68.40% and 34.50%. All within tolerance, 25 C larger, every p < 0.004. The first run had to map the criterion's 'all time points' and 'after inoculation' onto the data's seven days and asked; the answer names the readings by day, which drops the earlier reading (c), sum over days 0 to 12 (66.58% and 34.00%, now a variant) and adds the sum over days 2 to 12, which was a variant before. Under the new readings the outcome is unchanged. The variants over days 0 to 10 give 70.03% and 43.02% (trapezoid, 35 C outside tolerance) and 64.90% and 40.29% (sum, within); they decide nothing.

Repeated-measures ANOVA as Table S1b: temperature F(1, 18) = 32.746, time F(2, 36) = 86.963. Mean log10 PFU/ml 8.756 at 25 C, 7.375 at 35 C. Highest on day 4 (10.511 and 8.947, from 4.0 at inoculation), lower on day 12 (8.037, 6.859); the lowest is day 8 at both temperatures. The paper's text prints the time effect as F1,18 = 84.88, which is its sum of squares.

35 C +P, 0 of 4 replicates with mucoid colonies; 25 C +P, 1 of 4 (replicate 2, 700 of 71700 CFU/ml), the other three 100% SCV. Mucoid share of the 25 C +P treatment, mean of replicate frequencies, 0.244%, within 0.24 +- 0.024 (reading a1). From pooled counts (reading a2) it is 0.561%; reading (b), SCV share of the exceptional replicate, 99.02%. The paper calls the 0.24% the frequency of SCVs; in the data it is that of mucoid colonies. The first run asked whether reading (a) is a mean of replicate frequencies or a pooled share; the answer says the paper does not fix it and names both as readings (a1) and (a2) under the criterion's rule that one matching reading is enough. The outcome is unchanged, and the open choice is now a reading of the criterion, not a deviation.

Two-way ANOVA as Table S2, phage F(1, 12) = 7.016, p = 0.0212; mean SCV share 99.88% with phage against 64.83% without. Mucoid share without phage, mean of replicates, 15.34% at 25 C (outside 20 +- 2) and 55.00% at 35 C (within); pooled, 15.64% and 23.78%, both outside. The phage effect and the 55% hold; the 20% does not.

On unit means, phage F(1, 15) = 280.75 with sequential sums of squares (the paper's value; unit means with sequential sums of squares reproduce Tables S3a to S3c term by term) and 30.50 with type II, both p < 1e-4; the clone variant gives 973.58 and 51.76. The first run treated unit means and clones as readings; the answer fixes the unit as the mean of the clones of each colony type within each replicate population and makes clones a variant. findings.statement: The twitching sheet (Figure 2D) does not identify its clones. It has no morphotype column; its four 35_1 rows carry the names of four 35_0 SCV clones (6b6s1, 6b6s2, 6b8s1, 6b8s2) with different values, where the biofilm and disease sheets name the 35_1 clones 6b1s1, 6b1s2, 6b2s3 and 6b2s4; and in 25_0 the four mucoid names 6d5a2 to 6d8a2 appear twice with different values, where the other sheets have four SCVs.

The deposited twitching values do not reproduce Table S3d: with the colony types of the design, the residual sum of squares is 28.32 against 35.78 and the temperature sum of squares 2.48 against 3.857; only colony type x phage (27.04) and temperature x colony type (0.081) agree. The total sum of squares of the data is 72.28 against 82.08 summed from Table S3d, so no assignment of colony types reproduces it if its sums of squares are sequential, which the table does not state. Every other ANOVA the paper prints (Tables S1a, S1b, S2, S3a to S3c, S3e, S3f) is reproduced from the deposited data.

The variant table (snp_indel) gives, per variant and group of four sequenced clones, the number of clones that carry it, not which clones. Per-clone mutation counts and co-occurrence (for example whether the gspE and gspF mutations of 35 C +P SCVs are in different clones) cannot be read, and the genome reads are not public.

BioProject PRJNA1028400, named in the paper for the genomes of the evolved clones, has 28 BioSamples and 14 assemblies and no sequencing runs, so the reads the variant calls come from are not public. The RNA-seq reads are public in PRJNA1032726 (ten runs), though the Methods say they are shared on request.

The growth curves the maximum growth rates and carrying capacities were fitted to are not deposited, only one fitted value per clone, so the fits cannot be repeated and the model behind them (logistic, as the Methods say, or the code's best of four by AIC) cannot be checked. The pilB and pilM data of Table S6 are not deposited either.

The data disagree with statements of the text: SCVs form more biofilm than the ancestor in every clone (0.58 to 0.95 against 0.49 OD570), where the text says they retained ancestral-level biofilm; gspG is upregulated (log2FC 2.04) in the deposited DESeq2 table and Figure 4C list, where the text lists it as downregulated; phcS has log2FC 0.41, below the threshold under which the text calls it significantly upregulated; mucoid colonies are 15.3% at 25 C without phage, where the text says around 20%; and the 0.24% the text gives as an SCV frequency is the mucoid frequency of the 25 C +P treatment.

Small misprints in the paper's statistics, against the data: the area-under-curve ANOVAs are printed with df (1, 19) for 20 populations (the data give the printed F at df (1, 18)); the phage density time effect is printed in the text as F1,18 = 84.88, which is its sum of squares (F(2, 36) = 86.963 in Table S1b); Table S3e prints the temperature sum of squares as 0.346 for 0.3646; Table 1 places the RSc3091 deletion at C-432461, the variant table at 431461.

The OD600 values of Figure 1B include day 0 and negative values (eight, down to -0.029, at 25 C with phage), so they are blank-corrected and include the inoculation, neither of which the README or Methods says; the paper's ANOVA uses days 2 to 12. The README does not give units for the growth rate (headed maxgrowthrate(OD600)) or say that adsorption is a proportion.

In the carrying capacity sheet the ancestor's value (1.4355) is headed maxgrowthrate(OD600). The variant table's GENE column holds PROKKA names that differ from the paper's (phcS is sasA_8, pilD outO, gspE hxcR, gspF epsF_1); the gene_blast sheet gives the paper's names by locus tag. The Figure 4B list holds 11 genes where the paper speaks of 13.

disagreements.reason: Colony type F=42.37 with mucoid higher, and the ancestor (0.489) is below the mucoid IQR. But the ancestor lies below the SCV minimum (0.576): all 16 SCVs are above it and their mean is 47% higher. Both readings agree that SCVs within ancestral level fails (cell 54). The ancestor value is taken without checking how many anc rows exist; the outcome turns on it (B3).

phcR is up (log2FC 1.83) and pilD down (-1.35), and the other pilus and fimbrial genes are down. phcS is up but only by log2FC 0.41, below the threshold. Only 3 of the 11 listed Figure 4B genes meet both thresholds (at most 5 of 13) against the claimed 7 (cell 80).

The verifier agreed with all 32 outcomes and listed six statements the printed numbers did not support; each is recorded under the claim it bears on most closely (the R range under fig2a-phage-exposed-more-resistant, the RSc3091 position under table1-pild-in-25p-mucoid, the 25_0 strain names under fig2d-mucoid-25p-reduced-twitching, the Table S4 clause under sequencing-mutation-count).

entries.name: dryad-tdz08kq5d-wang-2024
entries.title: Phage selection and resistance-virulence trade-offs in Ralstonia solanacearum (Wang et al. 2024)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Wang, Wang, Yang, Lu, Fields, Xu, Shen, Wei and Friman (2024) on Dryad dataset tdz08kq5d, one workbook with the data behind each figure of the paper. It covers the selection experiment (bacterial and phage densities, colony types), the phage resistance, growth, twitching, biofilm and virulence of evolved clones, the variant calls of 28 sequenced clones, the phage adsorption assay and the transcriptome tables. The growth curves, per-clone variant calls, genome reads and the pilB and pilM data of Table S6 are not in the dataset.
